newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/2 in firm market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/2 in firm market.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up about 1/2 point overall, spurred on by strength in the U.S. Treasury market and two positive economic reports released this morning.
"We are feeling real strong," said one municipal trader. feeling real strong.
The 30-year long bond surged on Tuesday's data, moving up 1-8/32 at 95-7/32 to yield 7.01 percent.
The U.S. Commerce Department released seasonally adjusted data on durable goods orders for March, which showed a 3.0 percent decline.

The first quarter Employment Cost Index, an overall yardstick of how much it costs employers to pay and provide benefits for their workers, showed labor costs rose 0.6 percent. The employment cost index was predicted at up 0.9 percent, according to a consensus survey of economists by Reuters.
"There are no sellers out there," said a trader, who noted that there was strong demand from institutions and retail.
Another trader said there was strong follow through demand for certain maturities in the approximately $935 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey offering sold on Friday.
"And now I'm dusting off my secondary," he added.
Meanhwile, in the primary market, municipal bond sales for Tuesday were expected to total $1.6 billion in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $1.3 billion in 14 sales, with a $640 million NYC Municipal Water Agency deal through J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. topping the list.
In debt futures, the June Municipal contracts gained 1 to 113-18/32 and the June T-bond was 1-6/32 higher to 108-19/32. The MOB spread was at plus 159 ticks.
